settings.title: Kids Guide Muzzle Mouth Tape
settings.description: A comprehensive guide to help your child get the best sleep possible
settings.counter_title: SLEEP GOAL: QUIET NIGHTS, RESTFUL MORNINGS
settings.counter_description: Reality check: Mouth breathing and snoring are sleep saboteurs—destroying your rest, energy, and relationships. Your Goal: Use Muzzle Strips to silence the chaos.

settings.title: Before You Begin
settings.text: Kids' mouth taping is a new habit, not everyone gets it right first. That’s normal. It may take a few nights for your child to adjust. Practice makes perfect. The key to success is when and how it’s applied.

settings.title: Right before bedtime
settings.option_desc:
• Have your child lie down, close their eyes, and prepare for sleep.
  • Apply the tape gently over closed lips.
  • Hold firmly for 15 seconds. Avoid talking/moving afterward.

settings.title: After they fall asleep
settings.option_desc:
• Wait 1.5–2 hours (deepest sleep cycle).
  • Walk in quietly and apply tape while they are fully relaxed.

settings.step_title: Make sure your childs face and lips are completely dry (no lotion, no lip balm).
If needed, trim tape with scissors to fit their face.
Gently stretch the tape while placing it over the mouth.
Press and hold for 15 full seconds.
Avoid speaking or moving the face once applied.

settings.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
settings.bottom_description: The first few nights may not be perfect — that’s okay and expected. Consistency improves sleep quality, which reduces restlessness over time. Once the child adjusts, most families report better sleep, easier mornings, and increased willingness to continue taping.

settings.title: When It’s Working
settings.subtitle: You’ll know proper usage when:
settings.list_content:
• The tape stays on all night
  • Your child wakes feeling rested
  • No dry mouth in the morning
  • Less tossing/turning during sleep

settings.title: Start with clean, dry skin
settings.text: Oils, lotions, or even a little residual moisture can affect adhesion. A quick wipe with water and a gentle dry-off helps the tape stay secure all night.

settings.title: Press and hold for 15 seconds
settings.text: After placing the tape, gently press and hold to warm the adhesive so it bonds better and stays on during sleep. Once applied, avoid talking unless necessary, as it can loosen adhesion.

settings.title: Apply after they’ve fallen asleep
settings.text: Apply the tape during their deepest sleep (about 1.5–2 hours after bedtime). If they wake without it, this usually signals restlessness or difficulty adjusting, and applying it while asleep can help.

settings.title: Customize the fit if needed
settings.text: Every face is unique. If you’re using the adult Strong Hold version, you can trim the edges or widen the center opening for a more personalized feel.

settings.title: Keep it playful and positive
settings.text: For little ones, turning it into a “sleep challenge” or offering small incentives helps them stay engaged and reduces resistance during the adjustment period.

settings.title: Be consistent and give it time
settings.text: It’s normal to need time to adjust. With consistent use for 2–4 weeks and proper placement, it becomes smoother—especially for restless sleepers who may remove the tape while tossing and turning. Nasal breathing reduces restlessness over time, so stick with it.

settings.title: Still Struggling?
settings.text: It’s totally normal. Feel free to reach out via customer support — we’re here to guide you through the adjustment process.
